title: Superparamagnetic Nanoparticles for Lysosome Isolation to Identify Spatial Alterations in Lysosomal Protein and Lipid Composition
protocol: Place the 3-neck flask containing the reagents on the heating mantle.
Connect the reflux condenser to the opening in the center of the 3-neck flask.
Clamp the entire setup in the middle of the reflux condenser using proper-sized clamps.
Secure the clamp to a metal stand providing enough support to the setup.
Connect the inlet and outlet openings of the reflux condenser to the water flow.
Turn on the water flow, ensuring that water enters through the lower end and exits through the upper end.
Place a glass stopper on one of the two remaining openings of the 3-neck flask.
Insert the temperature probe through the remaining opening of the 3-neck flask and seal the opening.
Ensure the tip of the temperature probe is well immersed in the reaction mixture for accurate temperature reading.
Turn on the magnetic stirrer (35 × g).
Using a tube, slowly pass nitrogen gas (∼1 bar) into the 3-neck flask from the top.
Slowly remove the glass stopper connected to the 3-neck flask.
Leave it open for 5–10 minutes and let the nitrogen gas flow out through this opening.
Replace the nitrogen gas delivering tube with a balloon filled with nitrogen gas.
Place the glass stopper back and seal all joints using metal holders.
Monitor the level of nitrogen gas in the inflated balloon to ensure an air-tight setup.
Turn on the heating and set the temperature to 200°C using an external device for power control.
Maintain the temperature at 200°C for 2 hours.
After 2 hours, increase the temperature to 300°C using an external device for power control.
Maintain the temperature at 300°C for 1 hour.
Turn off the magnetic stirrer and heating.
Allow the black colored slurry to cool down to room temperature (∼20°C) undisturbed for about 1 hour.
Carefully release the pressure inside the 3-neck flask by slowly removing the glass stopper.
Disassemble the setup carefully.
Remove the magnetic stir bar from the slurry.
Add 300 mL of absolute ethanol to the slurry to precipitate SPIONs.
Transfer the contents from the 3-neck flask to 50 mL glass tubes.
Place the tube on a magnetic separation stand to separate SPIONs from unreacted chemicals.
Leave the tube undisturbed for 5–10 minutes.
Use a glass pipette to carefully remove large particles and unreacted chemicals that remain suspended in ethanol.
Remove SPIONs from the magnetic separation stand.
Re-suspend SPIONs in 40–50 mL absolute ethanol per tube.
Repeat steps until ethanol appears transparent after attracting SPIONs to the magnet.
Remove ethanol completely and re-suspend SPIONs in 20 mL hexane.
Centrifuge the tube at 4,100 × g for 10 min to remove aggregates.
Carefully collect the supernatant containing the SPIONs.
Transfer the collected supernatant into a glass vial with a screw cap.
Store the vial of SPIONs suspended in hexane at 4°C.
Clean Platinum-HT pans in piranha solution.
Flame the cleaned Platinum-HT pans until they are red hot before use.
Place two clean, empty Platinum-HT pans on the carousel of the auto-sampler.
Press TARE to bring the base weights to 0.
Place 100 μL of SPIONs suspended in hexane on each pan and wait for 3–5 min for the hexane to evaporate.
Heat the pans to 80°C to remove solvent traces.
Increase the temperature to 850°C with a heating rate of 20°C per minute.
Record the mass of the pans every minute until the temperature reaches 850°C.
Use Universal Analysis 2000, v 4.5A software to calculate the concentration of SPIONs.
Evaporate hexane completely from a 1 mL sample of SPIONs suspended in hexane on a weighing boat if TGA is not available.
Measure the dry weight of SPIONs after evaporation.
Wear appropriate PPE when handling particulate forms of SPIONs to avoid toxicity.
Use Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) to measure size and shape of SPIONs.
Wear appropriate PPE.
Place a small drop of SPIONs suspended in hexane on an amorphous carbon-coated copper grid.
Wait for 5–10 minutes at room temperature until the solvent evaporates.
Insert the sample holder with the grids into the TEM.
Acquire TEM images from each of several independent grids of the same sample.
Measure the diameter of SPIONs from each grid.
Take an average of at least 100 particles to estimate shape and size distribution.
Take 10 mg of SPIONs resuspended in hexane and transfer to a 50 mL glass centrifuge tube.
Evaporate the hexane completely.
Purge nitrogen into the tubes to fasten evaporation.
Re-suspend SPIONs in 1 mL of extra-dry toluene.
Weigh 200 mg of meso-2,3-dimercaptosuccinic acid (DMSA) and re-suspend it by adding 1 mL of anhydrous dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Vortex the DMSA-DMSO mixture vigorously to enhance re-suspension.
Add the DMSA-DMSO mixture to the glass centrifuge tube containing SPIONs resuspended in toluene.
Place the tube on an orbital shaker at room temperature for 72 hours.
Centrifuge the tube containing the reaction mixture at 4,100 × g for 10 min.
Discard the top phase containing unreacted DMSA and DMSO carefully without leaving traces of chemicals.
Re-suspend the bottom phase containing DMSA-coated SPIONs in 2 ml of milliQ water.
Vortex to uniformly suspend the SPIONs.
Place an LS Column on a SuperMACS™ II Separator.
Equilibrate the LS column by adding 1 ml of milliQ water and discarding the flow through.
Add 2 ml of resuspended DMSA-coated SPIONs on top of the LS column.
Let the SPIONs enter into the column.
Pipet the SPIONs up/down in the column if necessary to ease the flow.
Collect and discard the flow through.
Wash the column once with 1 ml of milliQ water.
Remove the LS column from the SuperMACS™ II Separator and place it on a stand away from the magnet.
Add 1 ml of milliQ water and insert the plunger to force-collect the magnetically bound SPIONs.
Add 1 mL of milliQ water and insert the plunger to force-collect remaining magnetically bound SPIONs.
Centrifuge tube containing DMSA-coated SPIONs at 4,100 × g for 10 min.
Measure pH of DMSA-coated SPIONs and adjust carefully to pH 7 using 1 M NaOH.
Resuspend DMSA-coated SPIONs to a concentration of 200 μg per mL in serum-free culture medium.
Slowly add 5 mL of DMSA-SPION containing medium to the culture dishes.
Place the culture dishes in the incubator at 37°C for 15 minutes (Pulse).
Remove and discard the DMSA-SPION-containing medium from the culture dishes.
Add 5 mL of fresh medium supplemented with 10% FBS to the culture dishes.
Incubate the culture dishes back in the incubator at 37°C for 4 hours (Chase).
Discard the media after the Chase period.
Wash the cells three times with 5 mL of acidic buffer (0.2 M glycine).
Place the culture dishes on ice and add 5 mL of ice-cold PBS-/-.
Scrape the cells from the culture dishes and transfer them to a 15 mL Falcon tube, one tube per dish.
Centrifuge at 180 × g for 10 minutes (4°C).
Discard the supernatant and place the tubes containing cell pellets on ice.
Add 1 mL of ice-cold homogenizing buffer (HB) to cell pellets collected from each 100 mm diameter culture dish.
Resuspend the cell pellets in at least 1 mL of HB to ensure no clumps are present.
Flush the cell homogenizer a couple of times with milliQ water and two times with 1 mL of HB before use.
Pass the cell suspension through the cold cell homogenizer to the other syringe and back, constituting one passage.
Repeat step 81 to a total of ten passages to ensure uniform homogenization of the cells.
Carefully remove one syringe and transfer the total cell lysate (TCL) to a fresh 15 mL Falcon tube.
Use the other mounted syringe to collect the remaining TCL that is present in the bore of the cell homogenizer and transfer to the same Falcon tube.
Repeat step for the other three cell pellets.
Centrifuge the TCL at 800 × g for 10 min (4°C).
Carefully collect the post-nuclear supernatant (PNS) without disturbing the pellet and pool all PNS in a fresh Falcon tube placed on ice.
Discard the last millimeters of PNS above the pellet to avoid contamination from nuclear debris, unbroken cells, and other remnants.
Facultatively centrifuge the collected PNS again at 800 × g for 10 min (4°C) to ensure it is free of cell debris remnants.
Equilibrate the LS column by adding 1 mL of HB.
Collect and discard the flow through from the equilibration step.
Slowly add the PNS on top of the LS column (maximum 7 mL).
Let the PNS pass through the column.
Collect and discard the flow through after passing PNS.
Wash the column once with 5 mL of HB.
Remove the LS column from the SuperMACS™ II Separator.
Place the LS column on a stand.
Add 3 mL of HB to the LS column.
Insert the plunger to force-collect the bound/magnetic fraction in a fresh Falcon tube.
Repeat step but with 1 mL HB and pool with the previous 3 mL.
Transfer the bound/magnetic fraction into a clean ultracentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge for 30 min at 20,000 × gavg (4°C).
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
The resulting pellet contains the isolated lysosomes.
Re-suspend the pellet in HB or PBS for biochemical or functional assays.
Re-suspend the pellet in 50 mM Triethylammonium bicarbonate (TEAB) for proteomics or lipidomics analysis.
